newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-THREE RIDERS FAIL BLOOD TESTS FOR DOPING. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-THREE RIDERS FAIL BLOOD TESTS FOR DOPING. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Three riders were thrown out of the Paris-Nice race on Monday after failing blood tests, the cycling's security and ethics commission said.

It said Frenchman Erwan Mentheour and Italians Mauro Santaromita (corrects spelling from "Santaronita") and Luca Colombo were not allowed to start Monday's second stage and had their licences suspended for 15 days.
The three riders will not get back their licences until they have undergone another blood test at a laboratory in Lausanne accredited by the International Cycling Union (UCI).

Marc Madiot, sporting director of Mentheour's team La Francaise des Jeux, said: "All my team were tested before the race, they were all negative and therefore authorised to start the race (on Sunday)."
The UCI said in January it was introducing blood tests before races to try to protect the health of riders and curb doping in the sport.
